script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Morning, Sarah. November 22nd already. Wow.
script.ja: おはようございます、サラさん。もう11月22日ですね。早いな。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Good morning, Alex. It's The Daily Tanu-chan Show. Feels like winter's really here now.
script.ja: アレックス、おはよう。ザ・デイリー・タヌちゃんショーです。もうすっかり冬って感じね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: It does. And that cold wind is something else. Good thing I had my coffee.
script.ja: そうですね。この冷たい風はきつい。コーヒー飲んできてよかった。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: I've got my tea. Anyway, did you see the news about the Gucci 'owl fan'?
script.ja: 私はお茶ね。ところで、グッチの『フクロウの扇子』のニュース見た？

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, the one that looks kind of traditional Japanese, but it's like, really expensive? I saw that.
script.ja: ああ、なんか日本の伝統的っぽいけど、ものすごく高いやつですよね？見ました。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Right. It's bafflingly expensive, isn't it? For an owl fan.
script.ja: そう。フクロウの扇子にしては、驚くほど高価よね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, bafflingly expensive. That's a good way to put it. I mean, my whole wardrobe probably costs less than that one fan. I'm a Uniqlo guy.
script.ja: ええ、途方もなく高い。まさにそんな感じですね。僕の全クローゼットの服より、あの扇子一枚の方が高いかもしれない。ユニクロ派ですから。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Some people like those kinds of things.
script.ja: ああいうのが好きな人もいるからね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: I guess. I just can't imagine spending that much. It's beyond my comprehension. Anyway, changing topics... I also saw the news about the sea otter.
script.ja: そうですよね。ただ、僕にはそこまで出すのは想像できない。理解の範疇を超えてます。ところで、話は変わるんですけど…ラッコのニュースも見ました。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: The last captive one in Japan, right? Kira, the 18-year-old female.
script.ja: 日本で最後の飼育ラッコね。18歳のメスのキラちゃん。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah. It's sad. Down from over a hundred decades ago to just one. It makes you think about endangered species.
script.ja: ええ。悲しいですね。数十年前は100頭以上いたのに、たった1頭になっちゃったなんて。絶滅危惧種について考えさせられます。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It's a serious issue globally. Not just here.
script.ja: 世界的に深刻な問題だから。日本だけじゃないわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: I suppose. Oh, and the JR East mascot news! They're keeping all three of the new characters. I thought they were just choosing one.
script.ja: そうですね。ああ、それとJR東日本のマスコットのニュース！新しいキャラクター3体全部残すって。1体だけ選ぶのかと思ってました。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: They decided to use all three, apparently. The Suica Penguin is still iconic, though.
script.ja: 3体全部使うことにしたらしいわね。でもやっぱりSuicaペンギンは象徴的よね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: He is. My little one loves mascots, actually. Points at all the ones on TV. It's funny.
script.ja: そうですね。うちの子、実はマスコットが大好きなんです。テレビに出てるの全部指差して。面白いですよ。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: They get excited by bright colors and simple shapes. My kids were the same.
script.ja: 鮮やかな色とかシンプルな形に興奮するのよね。うちの子たちもそうだった。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: It's nice to see that wonder. But it also means they pull at everything, so I'm always chasing them. My day-to-day can feel a bit... humdrum sometimes, just cleaning and chasing.
script.ja: その無邪気さを見るのはいいんですけど、何でも引っ張るから、いつも追いかけ回してます。僕の毎日はちょっと…退屈に感じることがあるんです、掃除して追いかけてるだけだと。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Humdrum? You mean like, boring or repetitive?
script.ja: ハムドラム？つまり、退屈とか、繰り返しの多いってこと？

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, exactly. That feeling when you're just doing the same things over and over. It's rewarding with the baby, of course, but also... a lot.
script.ja: ええ、まさに。同じことばっかり繰り返してる感じですね。もちろん、赤ちゃんとの時間はやりがいがあるんですけど、でも…大変で。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: That's parenting. It passes. You find ways to break up the routine.
script.ja: それが子育てよ。すぐに終わるわ。ルーティンを破る方法を見つけるの。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: I hope so. Speaking of work and daily life, today is 勤労感謝の日, right? Labor Thanksgiving Day.
script.ja: そうだといいな。仕事と日々の生活といえば、今日は勤労感謝の日ですよね？Labor Thanksgiving Day。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: That's right. It's a national holiday established in 1948. The idea is to appreciate labor, celebrate production, and express gratitude to each other.
script.ja: ええ、そうよ。1948年に制定された国民の祝日。労働を尊び、生産を祝い、国民が互いに感謝しあう、という趣旨なの。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, I didn't know that it was about celebrating production too. I thought it was just about thanking people for their hard work.
script.ja: へえ、生産を祝うという意味もあるんですね。ただ単に、みんなの労働に感謝する日だと思ってました。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It used to be called Niiname-sai before the war, which was an ancient harvest festival. They just changed the meaning and name after the war.
script.ja: 戦前は新嘗祭って呼ばれてたのよ。古代の収穫祭だったのが、戦後に意味と名前を変えただけなの。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: That's interesting. So it has roots in agriculture. I guess it makes sense, appreciating the fruits of labor.
script.ja: それは面白いですね。農業にルーツがあるんですね。労働の成果に感謝する、って考えると納得できます。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It does. It's a good reminder to reflect on what we do and how it contributes.
script.ja: そうね。自分たちが何をして、それがどう貢献しているか、考えるいいきっかけになるわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, especially with my job. Sometimes it feels like there's no clear demarcation between work and personal life, especially with the baby.
script.ja: ええ、特に僕の仕事だと。仕事とプライベートの間に明確な境界線、つまりデマケーションがないように感じます、特に赤ちゃんがいると。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Demarcation? You mean a clear separation or boundary?
script.ja: デマケーション？はっきりとした区切りとか、境界線のこと？

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Exactly. Like, where does work end and family time begin? Or even just my own time. It all just blends together.
script.ja: まさにそれです。どこで仕事が終わって、家族の時間が始まるのか？あるいは、僕自身の時間でさえ。全部が混ざり合っちゃうんです。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: That's common for young parents. You have to actively create those boundaries. It takes effort.
script.ja: 若い親にはよくあることよ。意識的にそういう境界線を作る必要があるの。努力がいるわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: I know. I try to make time for myself, even if it's just going to the public bath on the weekend. The sento, you know?
script.ja: 分かってます。週末に銭湯に行くとか、たとえそれだけでも自分の時間を作ろうと努力してます。銭湯、分かります？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Of course. The public bath. It's a good way to relax.
script.ja: もちろん。銭湯ね。リラックスするにはいいわね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, there's something about just being quiet, soaking in the hot water. I always feel refreshed, like I've hit the 'totonou' state.
script.ja: ええ、静かに、熱いお湯に浸かるのがいいんですよね。いつも、ととのった状態になったように、スッキリするんです。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It's a good escape from the noise. My son still goes with his friends sometimes.
script.ja: 喧騒から逃れるにはいいわね。うちの息子もまだ友達と行くことがあるわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: I can see why. It's a simple pleasure. Even just a short break makes a difference.
script.ja: 分かります。ささやかな楽しみですよね。ちょっとした休憩でも違いますから。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It does. So, for Labor Thanksgiving Day, what are your plans for expressing gratitude?
script.ja: そうね。じゃあ勤労感謝の日、アレックスはどうやって感謝を表す予定？

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, uh, I haven't really thought about it. Maybe just saying thank you to my wife for everything she does. That's probably the most important thing.
script.ja: ああ、えっと、特に考えてませんでした。たぶん、妻にいつもありがとうって伝えるのが一番大事なことですね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: That's a good start. Simple is best sometimes.
script.ja: いい始まりね。時にはシンプルが一番よ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah. Well, it's been a good chat, Sarah. I feel a bit more ready for the day after this.
script.ja: ええ。じゃあ、サラさん、いいおしゃべりでした。これで今日一日、ちょっと準備ができた気がします。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Have a good one, Alex. And enjoy your coffee.
script.ja: 良い一日を、アレックス。コーヒーも楽しんで。

wikipedia.description: 「勤労をたっとび、生産を祝い、国民が互いに感謝しあう」を趣旨として、1948年（昭和23）に制定された国民の祝日。戦前の「新嘗祭」の日付をそのまま「勤労感謝の日」に改めたもの。
